question: How is the AES-256 session key set up (NewAES handshake), and how are cut paths encoded and streamed to the machine?

resolution: RESOLVED on hardware 2026-11-20 over USB: the Maker accepts PLAIN (unencrypted) cutting. BeginDraw 0x21 ACKed (00 21 ...), nine MultiDrawVector 0x43 batches ACKed (00 43 ...). No AES session needed; the built-in key table is not copied. Flow control: each ACK's LAST byte is the machine's remaining buffer space, dropping ~0x38 (56 = one batch) per command; when it runs low the machine NACKs a batch (01 43 ...). Fix implemented in MatCraft Request::Cut: on a NACK, wait and resend the same batch (up to 90 s) until the buffer drains, matching the original's retry. ACK form is 00 <opcode> <..> <..> <space>; NACK is 01 <opcode> ... . Still open: mat origin/axes and tool/speed/pressure tuning for a clean cut, and whether a mid-run NACK can mean an error rather than a full buffer. AES key derivation remains intentionally unimplemented. BLADE ENGAGEMENT (traced, app/TOOL-PRESSURE.md): the firmware lowers the blade on cut vectors (kind 0x00) and lifts on travel (0x02) ONLY if pressure was configured first. Pressure is the final u16 BE of SetMachineState 0x30 in Z encoder counts; the setup order before BeginDraw is 0x30,0x31,0x37,0x3E,0x3F. MatCraft now sends these (setup_payloads/CutSetup) with a hand-tuned pressure field (Machine panel), since grams->counts needs the machine's calibration (read via A0) which is not decoded. First cut traced with NO setup, so no force. OPEN: the correct pressure count for a given material (tune by hand, or decode the A0 calibration to use grams). VECTOR KINDS (app/VECTOR-KINDS.md): the host emits only 02 move-to and 00 line-to for a straight cut, PLUS a terminal 02 move-to at the contour's last point (square = 02 00 00 00 00 02); kinds 03/04/09 are NOT used for a plain cut. MatCraft now appends that terminal move. The 03-line-in theory for the Z bobbing is unsupported — the host emits adjacent 00s with no lift. The actuator bobbing when pressure is raised is firmware Z-control behavior not visible in the host binary; the likely fix is a CALIBRATED pressure (grams->counts via the machine's A0 calibration table, funcs 0x4d6ba0/0x4d6f40/0x4d71f0; reply format undecoded) instead of a raw hand-tuned count. CALIBRATION IMPLEMENTED (app/PRESSURE-CALIBRATION.md): the machine's drag-blade pressure table is 16 Read-Persistent-Memory (A0) rows at indices 0x21..0x30; each reply has grams at bytes 7-8 and Z counts at bytes 9-10 (u16 BE). MatCraft now reads these at connect (Request::ReadCalibration), interpolates grams->counts the way the original does (single-precision linear, saturating at the ends), and the Machine panel sets pressure in GRAMS bounded by the machine's own range; the resulting in-range count goes in 0x30. This should stop the Z servo hunting that raw guessed counts caused. OPEN: confirm on hardware that the grams value cuts cleanly without bobbing, and the ±0.5mm more/less variant (A0 0xA3). ENGAGEMENT PARITY (app/CUT-INIT.md): even with calibrated in-range pressure the blade stayed light and the Z bobbed. Codex's full connect-to-cut transcript found three confirmed parity gaps MatCraft was missing and now sends: (1) a pre-setup EndDraw 0x22 before 0x30; (2) FOUR gated persistent-memory writes A1 005D=10000, 005F=75000, 0082=10000, 0084=75000 between 0x3E and 0x3F (CricutDevice.exe 0x48edc0; likely Z force/motor config); (3) the work area in 0x30 is the mat/job size 12x12, not the 2x2 design bounds. Full setup is now 22,30,31,37,3E,A1x4,3F,21,43..,22. OPEN (firmware boundary, unverified on hardware): whether these restore downforce and stop the bobbing; conditional homing F0 / tool-detect EA not yet added. TOOL PREP (app/TOOL-PREP.md): added the pre-setup tool prep MatCraft skipped — B9 position query, optional travel to Y=8.0, Home Theta F0 08 (initial drag-knife), Tool Detect EA (00 01 EA; reply 00 06 EA <tool-code> <4 samples>; EA is how the machine identifies/seats the tool). Speed profile confirmed CORRECT for drag selector 0; no Z-datum command exists in the host cut path. Codex: the per-segment Z bobbing cause is NOT in the host binary — it's the Maker firmware motion/Z-control loop. The prep (esp. EA) is the last source-backed lever; if the blade still bobs/too light after it, the host binary is exhausted and the next step would be capturing a real Design Space USB session to diff.
